## 0. The Assignment at a Glance

> ***"Design and run an end-to-end big data pipeline on a relevant use case, and present the insights you found."***

| 👥 Who | 🎯 What | 🛠️ How | 🎤 Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| You work **in groups**, as formed in class. Every member must be able to explain every part of the project. | A **data analysis of your choice** on Binance or TfL data (or another source), answering real business questions. | **NiFi** to ingest, **HDFS** to store, **Spark** to process and query: the architecture of the course. | A **presentation in the last class**, with a slide deck shared with your classmates, plus your NiFi flows and notebooks. |

**Think of it as the course in one project.** Labs 5.1 and 8.2 (ingestion), 8.1 (data lake), and 16.1, 17.1 and 18.1 (Spark DataFrames, EDA and SQL) are your templates.

### The pipeline you will build

```
SOURCES                      INGESTION (required)       STORAGE (required)             PROCESSING (required)                 RESULTS
Binance                      Apache NiFi                HDFS data lake                 Apache Spark · Jupyter notebooks
  REST · WebSocket · dumps   one flow per source        raw/       as ingested · JSON  ① Data engineering: raw → curated      💡 insights
TfL Unified API         ──►  InvokeHTTP           ──►   curated/   clean · typed ·  ─► schema · flatten · clean          ──►  📊 charts
  bikes · lines · arrivals   → Split / Merge                       Parquet             ② Data analytics: EDA · profiling     🎤 slide deck
Enrichment (optional)        → UpdateAttribute          analytics/ aggregated tables     DataFrames + Spark SQL              ✅ conclusions
  weather · holidays · open  → PutHDFS                                                   business questions
  data (JSON · CSV)
Optional, extra credit: a streaming path NiFi → Kafka (lab 8.2) · MinIO as an extra object store · Airflow / Kestra to orchestrate
```

### Technologies: required and optional

| Layer | Required | Optional, extra credit | Not accepted as a replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ingestion** | **Apache NiFi**: one flow per source, exported as a flow definition | **Kafka** streaming path (lab 8.2); **Airflow** or Kestra to orchestrate | Python scripts or manual uploads instead of NiFi |
| **Storage** | **HDFS**: data lake with raw / curated / analytics layers | MinIO, Parquet, Delta Lake | Local folders or a database as the only store |
| **Processing** | **PySpark** in **Jupyter**: DataFrame API **and** Spark SQL | window functions, joins with enrichment data, Structured Streaming | pandas on the full dataset |
| **Visualisation** | charts from **aggregated** Spark results | pandas, Matplotlib, Plotly, Superset, Grafana | screenshots of raw tables as "results" |

Everything runs in **OSBDET**, the course environment: NiFi, HDFS, Spark, Jupyter, Kafka and MinIO are already installed. pandas is welcome at the end of the pipeline: aggregate in Spark, then `.toPandas()` the small result to plot it.

## 1. Choose Your Scenario

You can get insights from **two scenarios** we know well from the labs, or from a source of your choice (with limited support from the professor).

### Scenario A · Cryptocurrency trading in Binance

| Data | Endpoint / stream | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Candlesticks (OHLCV) | `GET /api/v3/klines?symbol=BTCUSDT&interval=1m` · stream `btcusdt@kline_1m` | JSON arrays |
| Order book | `GET /api/v3/depth?symbol=BTCUSDT&limit=100` · stream `btcusdt@depth20` | JSON |
| Trades | `GET /api/v3/aggTrades` · stream `btcusdt@trade` | JSON |
| 24 h statistics | `GET /api/v3/ticker/24hr` · stream `btcusdt@miniTicker` | JSON |
| Pairs and rules | `GET /api/v3/exchangeInfo` | JSON |
| History in bulk | `data.binance.vision` daily and monthly dumps | zipped CSV |

- **No API key** is needed for public market data. Respect the request-weight limits: one call per pair every few seconds is plenty.
- **You've done it before:** lab 8.2 ingested `btcusdt@miniTicker` from the WebSocket into MinIO and Kafka with NiFi.
- **Market-data-only URLs** are useful if a network blocks the main domain: `https://data-api.binance.vision/api/v3/…` and `wss://data-stream.binance.vision:443/ws/btcusdt@kline_1m`.
- ⚠ **Watch out:** prices and quantities arrive as **strings**, and timestamps in **milliseconds since epoch (UTC)**. Cast and convert them in your engineering notebook.

### Scenario B · Public transport in London (TfL)

| Data | Unified API endpoint (`api.tfl.gov.uk`) | Refresh |
|---|---|---|
| Santander Cycles docks | `/BikePoint` | every few minutes |
| Line status (tube, DLR, Overground…) | `/Line/Mode/tube,dlr,overground/Status` | on change |
| Arrival predictions (bus, tube) | `/StopPoint/{id}/Arrivals` · `/Line/{id}/Arrivals` | ~30 s |
| Road disruptions | `/Road/all/Disruption` | on change |
| Air quality forecast | `/AirQuality` | daily |
| Historical bike journeys | `cycling.data.tfl.gov.uk` (usage-stats) | periodic CSV files |

- Every endpoint returns JSON. Register for a free **app key** in the TfL API portal to get higher rate limits, and keep it out of your exported flows.
- You know `/BikePoint` well from labs 5.1, 16.1 and 18.1.

![The TfL BikePoint API response in the browser](data:image/webp;base64,)

- ⚠ **Watch out:** values in `additionalProperties` are **strings**, `modified` is not your snapshot time, and London switches between GMT and BST.

### Scenario C · Your own source, and data to enrich your analysis

**Another source** (the professor's support is limited):
- It must be **ingestible with NiFi** (an API, or files you can list and fetch), and big or frequent enough to justify the architecture.

## 2. Define Your Use Case

You are free to choose the use case you like most, but it **must be relevant**.

> ***"As a [stakeholder], we want to know [question] so that we can [decision]."***

**Examples:**
- As the **Santander Cycles operations team**, we want to know **which stations run empty or full, and when**, so that we can **plan van rebalancing routes**.
- As a **retail trader**, we want to know **at which hours BTC/USDT is most volatile and liquid**, so that we can **time our orders**.

**A relevant use case has:**
1. **A real stakeholder** who would act on your answer.
2. **3 to 5 business questions**, measurable with your data (a number, a ranking, a trend).
3. **Feasibility:** the API gives that data, and you can collect enough of it. Start early, because data accumulates over time.
4. **A reason for big data:** many snapshots, many entities, several sources.
5. **Honesty:** say what your data can't answer.

⚠ **Avoid** "we analysed the data" with no question, and questions that a single API call can answer.

### Use case ideas · Binance

| Idea | Example questions | Data |
|---|---|---|
| 🕯️ **Candlesticks & volatility** | Which hours and weekdays move BTC, ETH and SOL the most? Range, returns, volume per hour. | `@kline_1m` · window functions |
| 📚 **Order book & liquidity** | How do spread and depth change during the day? How much BTC can you buy before the price moves 0.1%? | `/depth` every N seconds |
| 🔗 **Pairs correlation** | Do altcoins follow BTC? Rolling correlation of 1-minute returns: who leads, who lags? | several pairs · joins on time |
| 🐋 **Volume spikes & big trades** | When do unusually large trades appear, and what happens to the price in the next minutes? | `@trade` · percentiles |
| 💵 **Stablecoins** | Does USDT/USDC deviate from 1.00? How often, how far, and for how long? | `/ticker/24hr` · klines |
| 😨 **Price vs sentiment** | Do Fear & Greed index extremes come with higher volatility or volume? | enrichment · daily join |

### Use case ideas · TfL

| Idea | Example questions | Data |
|---|---|---|
| 🚲 **Empty and full stations** | Which stations are empty in the morning and full in the evening? Where would rebalancing help most? | `/BikePoint` every 5 min |
| 🔧 **Unavailable docks** | Lab 18.1 at scale: which stations have the most out-of-service docks, and does it persist over days? | `NbDocks − NbBikes − NbEmptyDocks` |
| 🌧️ **Demand vs weather** | How much do available bikes change on rainy vs dry hours, weekdays vs weekends? | + Open-Meteo · join by hour |
| ⚡ **E-bike adoption** | What share of available bikes are e-bikes, by area and hour? Where do they run out first? | `NbEBikes` vs `NbStandardBikes` |
| 🚌 **Bus arrival reliability** | How stable are arrival predictions on a busy line? Which stops have the longest gaps between buses? | `/Line/{id}/Arrivals` · ~30 s |
| 🚇 **Tube disruptions** | Which lines report disruptions most often, at what times, and for how long? | `/Line/Mode/…/Status` |

## 3. Build the Pipeline

### 3.1 Ingestion with NiFi

**Minimum:**
1. **One NiFi flow (Process Group) per source**, scheduled every minute, every 5 minutes or whatever your questions need.
2. Collect **continuously** for long enough to answer your questions, starting in the first phase of the project.
3. File names include the **collection time**, e.g. `bikepoint_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.json`.
4. Files are written to **HDFS** with `PutHDFS`, into the raw layer.
5. Flows are exported as **flow definitions (JSON)**, without credentials.

**Going further:**
- Convert JSON arrays to **JSON Lines** (Split + Merge), as in lab 16.1.
- **Handle errors:** retry, and route `failure` somewhere visible.
- Load a **historical backfill** (Binance dumps, TfL journey CSVs) with `ListFile → FetchFile → PutHDFS` (lab 8.1).
- Add a **streaming path to Kafka** next to the batch path (lab 8.2).
- Give an **enrichment source** (weather, calendar, sentiment) its own flow.

> ⚠ **Remember lab 5.1:** sensitive values (keys, passwords) are not exported with a flow. Document which ones must be filled in after an import.

**Your template:** the TfL flow of labs 5.1 and 16.1, with `PutHDFS` as the last processor.

![The TfL flow of labs 5.1 and 16.1 in NiFi](data:image/webp;base64,)

| Processor | Role |
|---|---|
| `InvokeHTTP` | call the API on a schedule (GET, URL with symbol / endpoint) |
| `SplitJson` · `ReplaceText` · `MergeContent` | array → one document per line |
| `UpdateAttribute` | `source`, `dataset`, `filename` |
| `PutHDFS` | write into the raw layer |
| `ConnectWebSocket` · `PublishKafka` | optional streaming path (lab 8.2) |

```
# PutHDFS · Directory (NiFi Expression Language)
/datalake/raw/${source}/${dataset}/${now():format('yyyy/MM/dd')}
# UpdateAttribute · filename
${dataset}_${now():format('yyyyMMdd_HHmm')}.json
```

### 3.2 Storage in an HDFS data lake

```
/datalake
├── raw/                       # as ingested, never edited
│   ├── tfl/bikepoint/yyyy/MM/dd/
│   │   └── bikepoint_yyyyMMdd_HHmm.json
│   └── openmeteo/weather/…/
├── curated/                   # clean, typed, Parquet
│   ├── tfl/bikepoint_status/
│   │   └── dt=…/part-0000.parquet
│   └── openmeteo/weather_hourly/
└── analytics/                 # answers to your questions
    ├── station_empty_hours/
    └── demand_vs_rain/
```

This follows the pattern from the course: `/<layer>/<source>/<dataset>/…`

**Minimum:**
- The three layers, with one folder per source and dataset.
- **Raw** stays in its original format; **curated** is **Parquet**, partitioned by date.
- Show it in your slides with `hdfs dfs -ls -R /datalake` and `hdfs dfs -du -h /datalake`.

**Going further:**
- Fix the **small files problem**: turn thousands of tiny JSON files into a few Parquet files per day.
- Compare sizes raw vs curated (in lecture 6.2, Parquet was 24× smaller than CSV).
- Use Delta Lake tables in curated, or MinIO as a second store.

> ⚠ **Never edit raw data.** If your cleaning has a bug, you can always rebuild curated from raw.

### 3.3 Notebook ①: data engineering (raw → curated)

```python
raw = spark.read.json("hdfs:///datalake/raw/tfl/bikepoint/*/*/*/*.json")\
           .withColumn("file", F.col("_metadata.file_path"))

status = (raw
  .withColumn("p", F.explode("additionalProperties"))                      # ① flatten
  .groupBy("file", "id", "commonName", "lat", "lon")
  .pivot("p.key", ["NbBikes", "NbEBikes", "NbEmptyDocks", "NbDocks"])
  .agg(F.first(F.col("p.value").cast("int")))                              # ② long → wide, typed
  .withColumn("ts", F.to_timestamp(                                        # ③ snapshot time
      F.regexp_extract("file", r"(\d{8}_\d{4})", 1), "yyyyMMdd_HHmm"))
  .withColumn("dt", F.to_date("ts"))
  .dropDuplicates(["id", "ts"]))                                           # ④ dedupe

(status.repartition("dt").write.mode("overwrite")                          # ⑤ Parquet
       .partitionBy("dt").parquet("hdfs:///datalake/curated/tfl/bikepoint_status"))
```

1. **Flatten** nested JSON with `explode` (labs 16.1, 18.1).
2. Go **long → wide** and **cast**: numbers as numbers, never as text.
3. Take the **time** from the file name, not from `modified`.
4. **Deduplicate**, because APIs repeat unchanged records.
5. **Write Parquet**, partitioned by date.

> ✓ **Prove data quality:** rows in vs rows out, nulls per column, min/max per numeric column, number of snapshots per day. Put the table in your slides.

For Binance, klines arrive as arrays: read them by position with `F.col("value")[i]`, cast prices to `double`, and use `timestamp_millis(openTime)`.

### 3.4 Notebook ②: data analytics (curated → insights)

Follow the EDA of lab 17.1:
1. **Metadata:** schema, size, samples, entities, metrics, dimensions.
2. **Profiling:** `summary()`, nulls, distinct values, most and least frequent values.
3. **Business questions**, one section each, using the DataFrame API **and** Spark SQL (temporary views, lab 18.1).
4. **Enrichment joins** (weather, calendar, sentiment).
5. **Save** the answers to `analytics/`.

```python
status = spark.read.parquet("hdfs:///datalake/curated/tfl/bikepoint_status")
status.createOrReplaceTempView("status")

empty_by_hour = spark.sql("""
  SELECT id, commonName, HOUR(ts) AS hour,
         ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN NbBikes = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100, 1) AS pct_time_empty,
         COUNT(*) AS snapshots
  FROM status
  GROUP BY id, commonName, HOUR(ts)
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20""")

# window functions: change since the previous snapshot
from pyspark.sql import Window
w = Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy("ts")
moves = status.withColumn("delta", F.col("NbBikes") - F.lag("NbBikes").over(w))

# plot only small, aggregated results
pdf = empty_by_hour.groupBy("hour").agg(F.avg("pct_time_empty")).toPandas()
```

*Both code examples were tested with PySpark on real TfL snapshots stored with this naming scheme.*

## 4. Results, Presentation and Deliverables

### What counts as an insight

💡 **An insight is a number, plus its context, plus a "so what":** "Between 8 and 9 am, 12 stations around Waterloo are empty over 40% of the time (in our data), so a rebalancing van there before 8 am would serve the morning peak." *(An illustrative example, not a real result.)*

⚠ **Not an insight:** "BTC price went up and down", "there are 797 bike points", a screenshot of a raw table.

- Use one chart per question, with a title that **states the finding**.
- Say **"% of what"** and the size of every group, and set minimum volumes.
- Compare: hours, days, stations, pairs, rain vs dry.
- State your **collection period** and its limits (a week ≠ a year).
- End with **recommendations** and what you'd do with more time or data.

> ✓ **Remember lab 17.1:** sanity-check every number before it goes on a slide.

### Presentation structure

| # | Section | What to show |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Problem description** | Context, stakeholder, decision and your 3–5 business questions. What type of analysis? |
| 2 | **Data sources** | Every source and endpoint, original format, refresh rate, collection period, volume collected |
| 3 | **Data ingestion** | Architecture diagram + **screenshots of your NiFi workflows**, schedules, file naming |
| 4 | **Data storage** | **HDFS directory structure** of your datasets, formats per layer, sizes raw vs curated |
| 5 | **Data processing** | How you process the data (engineering notebook) and how you **query** it (DataFrames, Spark SQL); data quality checks |
| 6 | **Project results** | One slide per question: chart + finding. Did you get any insight? |
| 7 | **Conclusions** | Recommendations, limitations, lessons learnt, next steps |
| 8 | **References** | APIs, datasets and licences, documentation, tools (including any AI assistance) |

- **The deck is shared with your classmates** in the last class, so make it understandable without you talking.
- **Everyone presents a part**, and anyone may be asked about any part of the pipeline.

### Deliverables

| Deliverable | Format |
|---|---|
| 🎤 **Slide deck** used during the presentation | PDF (plus the original file) |
| **NiFi workflows**, one per source | flow definition `.json`, no credentials |
| **Jupyter notebooks**: ① data engineering, ② data analytics | `.ipynb`, executed, outputs visible |
| 📄 **README** | team, use case, sources, collection period, how to run, HDFS tree |
| 🧪 **Data sample** (optional) | a few MB of raw and curated data |

- **Submit everything through Blackboard** before the due date your professor announces, as a single `.zip` named after your group.
- ⚠ **Before you zip:** remove API keys and passwords from flows and notebooks, then restart the kernel and **Run All** so the notebooks run top to bottom.
- **Recommended:** keep the project in a Git repository and link it in the README.

### How it will be evaluated (proposed rubric)

| Criterion | Weight | Excellent looks like… |
|---|---|---|
| **Use case & problem** | 15% | A real stakeholder, sharp measurable questions, justified sources |
| **Ingestion (NiFi)** | 20% | Working scheduled flows per source, good naming, error handling, enough data collected |
| **Storage (HDFS)** | 15% | Clean raw / curated / analytics layout, Parquet, partitioning, no small-files mess |
| **Data engineering (Spark)** | 20% | Correct types and nulls, flattening, dedup, quality checks, reproducible notebook |
| **Analytics & insights** | 20% | DataFrames and SQL, joins, clear charts, real insights with context and limits |
| **Presentation & teamwork** | 10% | Clear story, on time, every member masters the whole pipeline |
| **Extra credit** | + | Kafka streaming path, enrichment sources, Delta Lake, orchestration, original use case |

*Weights are a proposal; your professor confirms the final rubric.*

## 5. How to Work

### A roadmap in five phases

| Phase | What you do | Done when… |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · Use case** | pick a scenario, define the stakeholder and questions, check the APIs | ✔ one-page proposal |
| **2 · Ingestion** | NiFi flows per source, `PutHDFS` into raw, schedules on | ✔ data flowing |
| **3 · Engineering** | raw → curated Parquet: types, nulls, dedup, quality checks | ✔ notebook ① |
| **4 · Analytics** | EDA and profiling, questions with DataFrames + SQL, charts, enrichment | ✔ notebook ② |
| **5 · Story** | one slide per question, rehearse and time it, package the deliverables | ✔ presentation |

NiFi keeps collecting in the background from phase 2 until you freeze the analysis. **Start ingestion as early as you can:** you can't analyse days of data you didn't collect.

### Team roles and practical tips

| Suggested role | Focus |
|---|---|
| **Ingestion lead** | NiFi flows, schedules, monitoring the collection |
| **Data lake lead** | HDFS layout, naming, sizes, compaction |
| **Data engineer** | notebook ①, data quality |
| **Analyst** | notebook ②, SQL, charts |
| **Storyteller** | slides, rehearsal, README |

Everyone still has to master the whole pipeline. Some practical tips:

- **Collection needs a running OSBDET.** Agree on who keeps a VM collecting, and for which periods, and document any gaps.
- Combine a **live collection** with a **historical backfill** (Binance dumps, TfL journey files) if you need more history.
- Only switch on the services you need: NiFi + HDFS while collecting, Spark + Jupyter while analysing.
- Develop on a **sample** (one day), then run on everything.
- Keep the Spark UI open: big shuffles and slow stages show up there.
- Version notebooks and flow definitions in Git, and never commit keys.

### Checklist before you submit

- ✅ **Every source has a NiFi flow**, exported as JSON, scheduled and writing to HDFS raw.
- ✅ **The HDFS tree is clean:** `/datalake/{raw,curated,analytics}/<source>/<dataset>/`.
- ✅ **Types first:** no numbers as strings, and no `"NA"` disguised as values.
- ✅ **Summaries make sense:** min ≤ quartiles ≤ max, and parts add up to totals.
- ✅ **Time is right:** snapshot time comes from the file, and you state UTC vs London time.
- ✅ **DataFrames and SQL** are both used, and pandas never touches the full dataset.
- ✅ **"% of what" and group sizes** appear next to every rate, with minimum volumes set.
- ✅ **Every chart answers a question**, and its title states the finding.
- ✅ **Notebooks run top to bottom:** restart the kernel → Run All, with outputs saved.
- ✅ **No secrets, sources cited:** keys removed, and APIs, datasets and licences listed in the references.

### Frequently asked questions

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Can we store in MinIO instead of HDFS?** | HDFS is required. MinIO can be an additional store (extra credit). |
| **Can we download files by hand and upload them?** | No: ingestion must go through NiFi. A historical backfill can be loaded with NiFi from a local folder (lab 8.1). |
| **How much data is enough?** | Enough to answer your questions with confidence. Several days of snapshots is a good target for time patterns. Say what you have. |
| **Both scenarios at once?** | Yes, if the use case links them. One well-done scenario beats two shallow ones. |
| **Can we use pandas?** | Yes, on small aggregated Spark results for charts. Processing must be in Spark. |
| **Spark 3.5 (OSBDET) or Spark 4?** | OSBDET's Spark is fine. Mind the differences seen in class (ANSI mode in Spark 4). |
| **Can we use AI assistants?** | Follow IE's academic integrity rules and disclose any tool you used in the references. You must be able to explain every line. |
| **Our collection stopped for a day. Problem?** | No, as long as you detect it, document the gap and avoid conclusions that depend on it. |
